feature: Navigation pending — the pip, the track and the escalation screen (PR 1)
note: Every row is taken on Slow 4G, because on a local server a pending state lasts a frame and the sheet would photograph the page it landed on. The nav slot's pip is not here: it sits in the shell, outside <main>, which no verb in this runner reaches by design; probe:nav-pending presses it at both widths and measures its paint time instead. The direct-load fallback is not here either: a goto resolves at DOMContentLoaded, after the stream has replaced the screen, so the probe reads it with a frame watcher. Screenshot timing inside the 120-400ms window is not reliable enough to hold a row's pip or track, so the row tracks are proved by the probe's check 8, which presses a commander row and a set row and measures the track painting inside each, and its check 3 saves the button's track at DPR 1. The ghost link's row stays because its first frame holds the track at both widths. The overlay rows cover /commanders, a set page, /decks, /collection and /discover, each through a link inside <main>. /about is reached only from the shell's own account menu, so probe:nav-pending escalates to it instead (check 6).
